openai_corpus_screen.exact_statement_summary: For every epsilon>0 infinitely many n have more than n^(1-epsilon) totient preimages.
openai_corpus_screen.exact_scope_explanation: The manuscript defines g(n)=#{m>=1:phi(m)=n} and its first theorem (thm:totient) asserts exactly: for every real epsilon>0, infinitely many positive n satisfy g(n)>n^(1-epsilon). This matches the pinned target, which counts natural preimages by ncard; for positive n, allowing m=0 adds no preimage because phi(0)=0. The paper explicitly proves finiteness of every positive fiber and unboundedness of the constructed n. No stronger density or uniform-in-epsilon claim is needed.

openai_corpus_screen.exact_statement_summary: An injective infinite sequence of Gaussian primes exists with uniformly bounded successive squared norms.
family_titles: Uniformly bounded components of Gaussian-prime graphs.
openai_corpus_screen.exact_scope_explanation: The manuscript uniform component theorem and Lean fullMain exclude every injective infinite Gaussian-prime walk with a real uniform step bound. The pinned target positively asserts existence of such a walk with integer upper bound C on squared norm. In Gaussian integers Prime implies Irreducible, and norm(z-w)=|z-w|^2; an integer squared-norm bound yields a finite real distance bound. Thus MainEndpoint directly negates the target existence claim, while UniformEndpoint is strictly stronger. Axis primes and all associates are included. This is a counterexample-side candidate, not a proof of the published True-equivalence.

openai_corpus_screen.exact_scope_explanation: The manuscript all-degrees corollary and Lean allDegrees assert positive-density (d-2)-power-free values of each rationally irreducible integer polynomial of every degree d>=4 with no fixed prime (d-2)-power divisor. Positive density implies the target infinitude. The corpus includes powers-of-two degrees and either leading-coefficient sign, hence removes two restrictions of the target. The target Irreducible f over Z with positive degree implies primitive and rationally irreducible by Gauss; its existence-of-a-natural-input local condition is equivalent to a missing root class modulo p^(d-2). This concerns the corrected parts.ii condition, not the known-false allow_fixed_divisors variant.

openai_corpus_screen.exact_scope_explanation: The manuscript explicitly applies its quartic squarefree-density theorem to x^4+2, stronger than the pinned infinitude claim. Irreducibility follows by Eisenstein at 2. The local condition follows from input zero for odd primes (value 2) and input one for p=2 (value 3), with residue representatives usable as positive inputs. The theorem counts positive integer inputs; adding the natural input zero has no effect on infinitude. The corpus Lean allDegrees specializes to degree four and exponent two.
